# Cairn System Rules Summary

## Pulses
A pulse increases a cairn's height by the stride plus a bonus. The bonus equals how many complete strides fit into the current height (before any addition). This means taller cairns get bigger bonuses per pulse, causing growth to accelerate over time.

## Repeated Pulses
Each pulse must be calculated individually from the new height. You cannot use shortcuts—the bonus recalculates at each step because the height keeps changing.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks after a pulse occurs. The amount lost depends on the new height after pulsing, divided by the leak size. The leak applies to what you just gained, not what you started with.

## Drain Cycles
Each cycle consists of one pulse followed by a fixed loss (the drain). The cairn shrinks gradually over many cycles if the drain exceeds what each pulse adds. The effect compounds because the bonus from each pulse decreases as height decreases.

## Finding Origins
To reverse pulses and find starting height, you work backwards one pulse at a time. Each new height must satisfy the pulse equation: you must find what starting height would produce exactly that result.

## Merging
Two cairns combine into one using fractional shares (in tenths). Each cairn contributes a weighted portion of its height, plus a fixed tether amount. The final result is floored. The exact calculation requires applying shares to both cairns, then adding the tether before flooring.
